A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hyperparameter sweeps, fitted scaling laws and model-size extrapolation experiments, including image-generation results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the validation-loss comparisons and image-generation experiments.

M1.justification: The Cross-DiT architecture and procedures for fitting optimal batch size, learning rate, model size and validation loss remain unchanged. The revised explanation of gradient assumptions introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Panda-70M for video experiments and include the single-frame image-generation experiments in Appendix E. The new Appendix E pointer in Section 3 does not add task coverage.

E2.justification: The optimal-versus-fixed hyperparameter comparisons retain the same comparators, including the fixed batch size of 128 and learning rate of 2.5313e-4 in Appendix C. Added theoretical citations are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the 2,000-sample validation subset, 17-frame 256×256 video inputs, validation every 200 steps, constant learning rates, model scales, training-token budgets and fitting procedures. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, grid-search checks, larger-model extrapolations and optimal-versus-fixed fitting analyses are retained. The revised plots do not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: The statement of five experiments per compute budget in Section 4.1 is unchanged. Neither version adds seed information, empirical uncertainty estimates or significance tests; the gradient-variance discussion concerns unchanged theoretical assumptions.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their numerical values. Both report fitting MSEs of 4.31e-7 versus 2.35e-7 and the same 45.5% reduction; Appendix E retains predicted and actual image losses of 0.6414 and 0.6340. Plot revisions preserve the reported results and trends.

T1.justification: The unbiased-gradient, bounded-variance and smoothness assumptions, convergence bound and Appendix B proofs are mathematically unchanged. v2 explains the existing filtration inline instead of as a numbered equation, adds attribution and renumbers subsequent equations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about video scaling laws, optimal hyperparameter prediction and performance prediction across model sizes and budgets. The abstract's 40.1% inference-cost reduction claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: The gradient-noise/update-count trade-off and parameter-efficiency interpretations remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning constant learning rates, validation-loss evaluation, low-resolution smaller models and unexplored resolution/frame-rate effects.

D1.justification: Appendices A and D retain the same VAE, PixArt initialization, T5 encoder, data settings, model-scaling ratios and parameter/FLOP accounting. No implementation details or resource-access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds Herrera et al.'s Local Lipschitz Bounds of Deep Neural Networks and Wang et al.'s Adapting to Smoothness. It also explicitly attributes gradient assumptions to the already cited McCandlish et al. The broader research positioning in Section 5 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 3 and 4 receive clearer titles, Section 3.1 rewrites the explanation of the filtration and assumptions, and Section 3 adds an Appendix E pointer. Other edits refine wording and cross-references while retaining the document's organization.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 revise the 3D viewpoints, axis labels and observation legends. Figure 5 changes a loss-axis label, and Figure 6c changes compute-axis tick labels. All nine figures and nine tables remain, with limited spacing and page-flow changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and traceability through the explicit filtration explanation in Section 3.1, added attribution, more specific equation references in Appendix B.3 and clearer observation legends in Figures 2–3. The scientific evidence and stated limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
